title: Fill Monday and Thursday in a snap-lid weekly pill organizer, holding the strip while each lid is lifted and snapped
keywords: pill organizer, weekly pill box, snap lid, medication, older adults, carer, fingernail lift, two hands
instruction: Put one caplet in Monday and one in Thursday of the pill organizer, leaving every lid snapped shut and the other days empty.
context: Weekly pill organizers are filled every week by millions of older adults and the family members who care for them. Each day's lid is hinged at the back and held shut by a small snap: you get a fingernail under the ledge at its front and lift until it pops, swing it up past upright so it stays open, drop the pill in, then swing it down and press it until it clicks. The organizer is a light plastic strip, so lifting a ledge lifts the whole strip unless the other hand holds it down. A lid left resting shut but not snapped spills in a bag, and a pill in the wrong day or two in one day is a medication error. The hard part is physical: a fingertip has to catch a 2.5 mm ledge and lift it while the other hand holds a 35 g strip, then the pill goes into a cell barely wider than the fingers.
setup: Positions in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Pill organizer: an extra-large weekly (7-day) snap-lid pill organizer such as the Ezy Dose Weekly Pill Planner XL (listed 7.4 x 1.5 x 0.9 in: 188 x 38 x 23 mm), translucent polypropylene, about 35 g, lying loose on the bare table (friction about 0.4), long axis along y, footprint centre at (0.190, -0.013), lids toward the robot's side as in the photo. Seven compartments in a row at a 26.9 mm pitch, each 25.8 mm wide, 35.6 mm front to back and 20.3 mm deep inside; walls 1.2 mm, dividers 1.0 mm. Reading from the robot's side, left to right, the lids carry the capitals S M T W T F S, so Sunday is at y +0.067, Monday +0.040, Thursday -0.040 and Saturday -0.094. Each lid is 1.5 mm thick and hinged along the back top edge; it opens to about 110 degrees, where it rests past upright. A tongue 12 mm wide hangs 9 mm down from the lid's front edge over the front wall and ends in a fingernail ledge 2.5 mm proud and 1.2 mm thick (its underside 12.5 mm above the table). A rounded hook on the inside of the tongue sits 0.3 mm under a rounded catch ridge on the front wall (overlap 1.3 mm). Lifting the ledge with about 1.6 N rides the hook over the catch at about 4 degrees open; pressing the lid's front edge with about 1.6 N (about 3.4 N at mid-lid) snaps it back (estimates; the rounded snap is symmetric, so opening and closing take the same force at the same point). All seven lids start snapped shut and every compartment is empty. (2) Caplets: three white film-coated multivitamin caplets (oblong, 19 x 9 x 7 mm, 1.3 g each), lying flat on the table with their long axis along x, at (0.085, +0.045), (0.085, -0.045) and (0.085, 0.000); one more than needed. Both arms start at the ready pose with grippers open.
scoring: Judged once both grippers have let go (each gripper's centre point between the pads at least 30 mm from the organizer's bounding box, lids included) and the organizer, its lids and the caplets have been still for 1 s (each moving under 0.5 mm and each lid under 0.25 deg per 50 ms step). A caplet counts for a day if its centre lies inside that compartment: within the inner walls and below the rim. A lid counts as snapped if its hook is below the catch (hook centre at least 0.5 mm below the catch centre); in a real trial, hold the organizer upside down for 2 s and a snapped lid stays shut. 1.0: exactly one caplet in Monday and one in Thursday, no caplet in any other day, all seven lids snapped, and the organizer flat (within 3 deg) within 30 mm and 3 mm of height of where it lay. 0.75: the same, but one lid not snapped. 0.5: exactly one caplet each in Monday and Thursday and none elsewhere, with two or more lids not snapped or the organizer moved more than 30 mm or tilted. 0.25: exactly one caplet in only one of Monday or Thursday with that lid snapped, nothing in any other day. 0.0: anything else, including any caplet still held or moving. Sticky zeros, whatever the end state: a caplet at any moment inside a compartment other than Monday or Thursday, two caplets at any moment inside one compartment, the organizer tipped more than 45 deg, or the organizer or a caplet off the table (more than 20 mm below its top). In a real trial the sticky zeros are judged from the overhead video.
run_limit: 3,000 steps (150 seconds at 20 Hz), about 2.5x the scripted demo's 61 s (1,212 steps)
reset_notes: Tip the caplets back out and lay them flat at their three marks, long axis pointing away from the robot; snap all seven lids shut; set the organizer back on its outline with the lids toward the robot.
fidelity: Organizer, lids and caplets are rigid primitives. The real snap's flex is in the lid's tongue; here the tongue is rigid and the catch ridge on the front wall is a 2.5 mm sprung slide (1.2 kN/m, 0.2 N preload), giving about 1.6 N to lift or press at the front edge (estimates: no maker figure). Inner sizes, the tongue, ledge and catch, and the 35 g mass are estimates from the listed outer size and maker photos. Lid letters are raised white strips. Caplets are flat-sided stadiums.
